# A1 — Does one job title hide several distinct roles?

*Draft, 2026-10-18 (panel day 42). Numbers are generated by `python -m analysis.a1_clustering`
(and `--family software_engineering`); the JSON behind every figure is in `report/a1_*_results.json`.*

## Answer in one paragraph

**Partly, and less cleanly than a taxonomy suggests.** Skill requirements do have real
co-occurrence structure: at every k from 2 to 10, the clustering beats a null model that keeps
each skill's frequency and each posting's skill count but scrambles which skills go together
(z = 26–40). But that structure is graded, not discrete. The gap statistic never reaches a
stopping point, absolute silhouettes are weak (≤ 0.15), and no partition is more than moderately
stable under resampling (bootstrap ARI ≈ 0.4–0.5 at every k). Of the five clusters at the most
stable k, **two are genuine role archetypes that span employers**: data/analytics and
cloud infrastructure. In the infrastructure one, **22 of the 47 postings are titled
"software engineer"**, which is the clearest case of a title hiding a role. Two more clusters are
mostly one employer's tech stack (Okta, GitLab), and one is unstable residue. The failure mode the
plan warned about shows up, but in its *employer* form, not its seniority form: cluster membership
is as strongly associated with **who is hiring** (Cramér's V 0.46) as with the job title (0.49),
and far more than with seniority (0.24).

## Data

- Technical IC postings (`in_scope()`: SWE, SRE/infra, data, ML, QA, security; not managers or
  interns), all postings seen 2026-09-07 → 2026-10-18: **270**.
- **Merged 57 exact duplicates** (same company, identical skill set; mostly one role reposted
  per city), giving **n = 213**. Left in, those copies form artificially tight clusters and inflate
  both silhouette and stability.
- Features: the 108 skills present in ≥ 5 postings, as a binary matrix, TF-IDF weighted, compared
  by cosine (spherical k-means on L2-normalised rows).
- The sample is concentrated. Okta is 51% of in-scope postings; Okta + MongoDB + GitLab are 81%.
  There are no junior in-scope postings at all.

## Method, and why each choice

| Choice | Why |
|---|---|
| TF-IDF + cosine, not raw Euclidean | Binary, sparse, high-dimensional; plain Euclidean distance would be dominated by how many skills a posting lists. |
| No UMAP before clustering | With 108 features and n = 213, there's no dimensionality problem to solve, and UMAP distorts densities, which would make the silhouette comparison against the null meaningless. |
| **Curveball null** (50 draws) | Random binary matrices with *both* margins fixed. A column shuffle keeps only skill frequency; skills-per-posting drives cosine similarity, so that weaker null would flatter the real data. |
| Gap statistic with the curveball null as reference | A uniform reference is meaningless for binary data; the null above is the right "no structure" baseline. |
| **k chosen by stability**, not by the gap rule | The gap rises through k = 10 without stopping, so the rule picks nothing. The k whose partition survives resampling is the one worth naming. |
| Bootstrap ARI + per-cluster Jaccard (100 resamples) | ARI says how stable the partition is; Jaccard says *which* clusters are real (≥ 0.75 stable, ≤ 0.5 dissolving; Hennig's convention). |
| **Company-capped resampling** (≤ 15 per employer) | Tests whether a cluster survives when no employer's volume can carry it. |
| Cramér's V against company, seniority, title family | The plan's failure check, extended to the confound this sample actually has. |
| NPMI for skill pairs (co-occur ≥ 5) | Raw co-occurrence would just rediscover that Python and AWS are common. |

## Results

![k curves](figures/a1_all_in_scope_k_curves.png)

**Is there structure at all?** Yes. The observed silhouette is 3.2–6× the null mean at every k
(e.g. k = 5: 0.127 vs 0.026 ± 0.003). With 50 null draws, p = 0.02 is the smallest p-value the test
can report, and every k reaches it.

**Is it a small number of clean groups?** No. The gap keeps rising through k = 10, absolute
silhouettes sit below 0.25 (conventionally "no substantial structure"), and bootstrap ARI is flat
at about 0.4–0.5 across k. The most stable k is 5 (ARI 0.49, 95% 0.30–0.65 over 100 resamples), but k = 4–8 are all
within noise of it. This is a continuum with a few denser regions, not a set of distinct jobs.

**The five clusters at k = 5:**

| # | n | Signature (prevalence, lift) | Titles inside | Employer mix | Jaccard: bootstrap / company-cap | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 30 | Tableau 53% ×6.7, dbt 33% ×7.1, statistics ×7.1, Snowflake ×5.1, ETL 50% ×4.1, SQL 73% | 17 data analyst, 4 data eng, **8 "software engineer"** | Okta 30%, Airbnb 20%, Stripe 17%… | 0.69 / 0.68 | **Data & analytics archetype**: stable, spans employers |
| 1 | 47 | Go 87% ×2.7, Kubernetes 87% ×2.4, Terraform 55% ×2.6, networking ×4.5, AWS/GCP/Azure | **22 "software engineer"**, 20 SRE, 3 QA, 2 security | Okta 53%, MongoDB 23%, Twilio 9% | 0.67 / 0.59 | **Cloud infrastructure archetype**: the clearest "title hides the role" result |
| 2 | 43 | GenAI ×3.5, Salesforce ×3.3, AI agents 72%, LLM 56%, JS/TS | mostly SWE, 6 ML | Okta 35%, MongoDB 26%, other 16% | 0.48 / 0.45 | Unstable mix (AI features + business systems) — not a role |
| 3 | 67 | React 51%, Java 73%, identity 58%, TypeScript, code review | 61 SWE | **Okta 78%** | 0.51 / **0.34** | Okta's product-engineering template; collapses once Okta is capped |
| 4 | 26 | Rails 69% ×8.2, Ruby 92% ×6.0, event-driven, PostgreSQL | 23 SWE | **GitLab 81%** | 0.75 / 0.73 | Stable, but it is one employer's stack, not a market-wide role |

![cluster by employer](figures/a1_all_in_scope_cluster_by_company.png)

**Within "software engineering" alone** (n = 144 after merging duplicates), structure is weaker:
best k = 3, ARI 0.40 (0.15–0.67). Clusters are a GitLab Ruby group, a JS/TypeScript/AI-features
group and a Java/cloud backend group. Company explains membership far more than seniority
(Cramér's V 0.56 vs 0.22).

**Skill associations** are mostly tight pairs (CSS + HTML, Android + iOS, Rails + Ruby) plus two
coherent stacks: data (Tableau, statistics, Presto, dbt, Snowflake, Spark) and GenAI (RAG, vector
DB, LangChain, prompt engineering).

![skill pairs](figures/a1_all_in_scope_skill_pairs.png)

## What this does and doesn't show

- **Shown:** within this panel, "software engineer" covers at least one distinct, stable,
  cross-employer role (cloud infrastructure) and some data roles. A posting's title alone
  under-describes it.
- **Not shown:** a clean 3–5 role taxonomy. Forcing one would mean naming clusters that dissolve
  under resampling or that are one company's template.
- **The employer confound is the real finding about the data.** With half the sample from one
  company, any skill-based segmentation of this panel partly recovers employers. A6 (geography) and
  A3 (drift) should report company-balanced estimates for the same reason.

## Threats to validity

1. **Employer concentration** (above). The company-capped stability test is the mitigation; it
   reduces the problem but can't remove it with only ~10 employers.
2. **Mention ≠ requirement.** Skills come from a regex dictionary over the full description
   (boilerplate removed); "partner with SRE teams" still counts as `sre`.
3. **Title assignment uses the rules classifier.** On 150 labelled titles it is 95% right on family
   with 98% precision and recall on the scope filter; Gemini was no better (McNemar p = 0.63), so
   the rules stay. The score is in-sample; a holdout check is still to come.
4. **Small n.** 213 postings and 108 features; the per-cluster tables rest on 26–67 postings each.
5. **Cross-sectional over six weeks.** Postings open at any point in the window are pooled.

## Reproduce

```bash
pip install -e '.[analysis]'
python -m analysis.a1_clustering
python -m analysis.a1_clustering --family software_engineering
```

Seed 20261018; 50 null draws, 100 bootstrap and 100 company-capped resamples.
